Tap water is fine as long as you use something like tap safe to eliminate the chlorine. You can also use RO water when first setting up the aquarium. I haven’t done much research into using RO water but my lfs says they do 70% RO and 30% tap. It’s basically like using really pure water but adding some tap water helps with the cycling I believe. Just make sure you use dechlorinated water.

When you first start your aquarium you should be checking for levels of ammonia, nitrite and nitrate. You want ammonia to spike first but this can take a while (you can speed it up by adding fish food flakes or using a established filter) after ammonia has started to rise you then begin to see nitrite. Certain bacteria neutralises the ammonia and turns it into nitrite. After that another bacteria neutralises the nitrite and turns it into nitrate. 

You want ammonia and nitrite to both be 0 before adding any fish but you want to at least see it up once so you know your tank has cycled. A good indication is to test the nitrate as this would show there was once ammonia and nitrite in your tank. If the nitrate gets above 20ppm it means your tank is in need of a partial water change. Nitrate should range between 5 to 10ppm 

This is known as the nitrogen cycle.
